To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cathodic arc deposition combined by macroparticle filtering is a versatile and efficient method to tailor the properties of amorphuous hard carbon films.
the bias voltage applied during cathodic arc deposition of hard carbon films is a very effective parameter to tune the mechanical properties of the films.
the mechanical properties of amorphouss carbon films can be tuned by the bias voltage applied during deposition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of bias voltage and substrate temperature on the mechanical properties of amorphuous hard carbon films.
the development of hard carbon films with tailored mechanical properties and the investigation of their microstructural origin.
the mechanical properties of amorphuous hard carbon films and their interfaces with respect to the bias voltage during deposition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hardness of cathodic arc carbon films can be tailored in the range between 30 and 80 GPa, the elastic recovery in the range between approximately 30 and 90%, and the elastic modulus in the range between approx. 150 and approx. 400 GPa.
the mechanical properties can be tailored to the needs by varying the deposition conditions.
cathodic arc deposition is a versatile method for the preparation of hard amorphous carbon films with a high degree of reproducibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a hard carbon film deposited at low bias voltage (−20 V) has the highest hardness and a film deposited at high bias voltage (−100 V) has the lowest hardness.
the mechanical properties of the hard amorphous carbon film are determined by the properties of the soft amorphous film.
by increasing the bias voltage the hardness of the films increases, whereas the elastic modulus decreases and the residual stress becomes compressive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties can be controlled by the bias voltage during deposition.
the mechanical properties of cathodic arc deposited amorphous hard carbons can be tuned over an extremely wide range by controlling the bias voltage.
by using cathodic arc deposition combined pulsed biasing, a large range of film properties can be obtained, including high hardness, low elastic modulus, low friction and low residual stress.
